question: In a certain code language, ‘DAINTY’ is written as ‘GCKQWB’ and ‘PROMISE’ is written as ‘SUQPKVG’. How will ‘CERTAIN’ be written in that language?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9b1ef5af07dc7cdface0347994bbc6f824cbda2bac27bcab0cb4cf07968dfa00.png] 

The logic followed here is:

**Logic: Vowels + 2, Consonants + 3.**

For, 'DAINTY’ is written as ‘GCKQWB',

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5552803c9722c894900cd319c447b22c0a6726d3657e46e69b4987abd54d8286.png] 

For, 'PROMISE’ is written as ‘SUQPKVG',

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/48b001db82fab82a03412850ceac3767e01ae0cbb973eb973c524a689fee2e07.png] 

Similarly, for '**CERTAIN**'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3f1996e5a30ae84fa3a517ad3e4ed0a14e2720d3ca4579daecee2dc56c443053.png] 

So, 'CERTAIN' will be written as '**FGUWCKQ**'.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".
